title: A Roman Emperor Taxed Pee. "Money Doesn't Stink" 🪙
caption:
A Roman emperor taxed PEE 🪙
Wait for the ending 👀

True story. Roman cloth-cleaners used urine to whiten wool, and Emperor Vespasian taxed it. According to the historian Suetonius, when his son Titus objected, Vespasian held a coin to his nose and asked if it smelled. The saying "pecunia non olet", money doesn't stink, comes from it.
What's the weirdest tax you know? 👇
first_comment: Two thousand years later, French public toilets are still named after him. Legacy. 🪙👇
